subject: missing levels in polytomous mirt: work around with a caveat

messages.author: 2d98f40c09e307a5
messages.subject: missing levels in polytomous mirt: work around with a caveat
parts:
If you are studying surveys with polytomous responses in samples that are not very large, it is to be expected that some item levels may not be observed.  This causes mirt to halt and burp out an error message.  I contacted Dr. Chalmers directly.  He suggested that I recode the data  so that no levels are missing.  This certainly works, but makes comparison of surveys were the level is missing with surveys where the level is present difficult.  I devised a work around which gives correct results.  HOWEVER, Dr. Chalmers points out that several diagnostic statistics will get confused by the dodge (see end of post).  Below you will find text of my exchange with Dr. Chalmers.

Hi Dr. Chalmers,

I have run into a problem using mirt, and I can't find a fix in the documentation.  I have thrashed around a bit and come up with something that might work.  So I am going to ask a long question which may have only a one word answer.

My colleague and I are trying to analyze a survey on student epistemic beliefs.  There are 14 questions (items).  All questions have potential responses of {1,2,3,4,5}.  This is a ordered agreement scale like a Likurt scale. My difficulty is that for some items, certain levels are not observed in the data set, and an error is generated when the mirt function is called:

> m.EB.1=mirt(EB,3,itemtype = "graded")
Error in FUN(newX[, i], ...) : 
  Items contain category scoring spaces greater than 1.
                    Use apply(data, 2, table) to inspect and fix

If I add a dummy row of data to the data set so that all levels are present in the data set for all items, mirt runs fine.

> dummyrw=c(1,1,1,2,1,1,1,1,1,2,1,1,1,1)
> tst1=mirt(rbind(EB,dummyrw),3,itemtype="graded")
Iteration: 254, Log-Lik: -1914.921, Max-Change: 0.00010
> summary(tst1)

Rotation:  oblimin

Clearly, I have identified the problem, but I can't use this output, because my dataset is contaminated by the dummy row.

I need a mechanism to specify to mirt what the levels for the items are without influencing the estimate.  Thrashing around a bit, I devised a possible code script.  It runs, and gives plausible output.  I don't know if this is actually a valid way to solve this problem.

What I have done is to create an internal data set using the large=T argument.  I then manually changed the frequency of my dummyrow's data pattern to 0, and then reran the mirt using the altered internal data.  This runs, and gives factors that are distinct from the factors from the augmented data set.  Also, when I predict fscores, I get the correct number (125) rather than the 126 I get when I predict from the mirt on the augmented data without going through the frequency adjustment.  All of these are hopeful signs, but without knowing how the internal data is used in the mirt calculations I don't really know if what I have done is correct.

So here is my question.  Is this a workable approach?.

Thanks a bunch.
Dr. Chalmers reply to me below:

There are a couple of things to do here, but what I would recommend is to change all 1's in $Innate_10 to 2's; this will preserve the 1 space ordering, and will make mirt happy (and still treats the data are ordered, which seems to be the requirement here). Just keep in mind that doing things like fscores(mod, method = 'EAPsum') won't be too meaningful anymore, and fit statistics like the S_X2 that are based on the total scores are not invariant to the type of data transformation. Otherwise, if you don't care about those two stats, then all other methods should be invariant to transforming the data this way (ordinal is ordinal, whether it starts at 1 or 100).

This is a good question actually, and no doubt other will run into the same issue and wonder why mirt throws a seeminly odd warning. If you'd be so kind, would you mind forwarding this email to the google forum
